messages:
ellie: quick q — for critical bugfixes that don't change the public API, do we always increment the PATCH and pin downstream, or are there cases where we should rollforward (bump MINOR) and rely on semver ranges? need a simple oncall playbook.
sam: short answer: prefer PATCH + pin for public packages we ship. rollforward (i.e. bump minor) only for deliberate additive features. for internal services we sometimes allow compatible rollforwards (caret ranges) if the consumers are tightly coupled and owned by the same team.
mario: +1. high level guidance: PATCH = bugfix/backwards-compatible perf/security; MINOR = new non-breaking features; MAJOR = breaking changes. we also need explicit rules for deps-only upgrades and autogenerated client changes.
jun: what do we do about tagging metadata for hotfixes? do we create special hotfix tags or reuse the release tag and increment patch?
deploy-bot: ci: created tag release/v1.23.5-hotfix.1 by @sam (CI build 7865) — pushed to origin and queued canary deploy.
sam: proposal for tag formats: canonical: release/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. for hotfixes: release/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-hotfix.N (hyphen) — hyphen plays nicer with tooling. for experimental/rc tags: release/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-rc.N or ci/release/v...

sam: example commands we use in CI:
```
git tag -a release/v1.23.5 -m "patch: fix kv-cache regression"
git push origin release/v1.23.5
```

sam: and for an urgent hotfix:
```
git tag -a release/v1.23.5-hotfix.1 -m "hotfix: fix nvlink OOM on startup"
git push origin release/v1.23.5-hotfix.1
```
ellie: ok on the hyphen. prefer hyphen over plus/metadata because some clients parse + as build metadata and strip it; hyphen is more predictable.
mario: we should also require a one-line changelog entry for every patch/hotfix and a backport checklist: 
- link to PR
- tests added or reason why not
- oncall/owner signoff for risky infra changes

jun: also clarify when to skip PATCH and go MINOR: if you're adding non-breaking public API surface that downstream SDKs will consume, do MINOR. if it's behind a flag or opt-in, PATCH is OK if it's strictly bugfix/perf/security.
sam: i'll draft a 1-page playbook: semver rules + tag conventions + CI validation script to reject malformed tags. will add a simple regex check in CI like: `^release\/v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?(-rc\.\d+)?$` and a changelog check.
ellie: :thumbsup: also decision: deploy-bot auto-rollback behavior? should the bot rollback to previous PATCH tag when healthchecks fail?
deploy-bot: Auto-rollback policy: enabled for canary and prod. if healthcheck failure rate > 1% sustained for 3 minutes, rollback to previous stable tag (the one the deploy job recorded). rollback triggered: release/v1.23.4.
mario: sounds good. please make sure the rollback event includes the failing metrics link in the deploy notification.
sam: noted. i'll include a sample notification payload in the playbook and add the regex check to CI. pinging @release-managers for a quick review when ready.
ellie: thanks — this is exactly what we needed. i'll update the release channel README with the playbook link and the CI check reference.
